description: DRC's trade dependency on China and the reverse flow of Chinese goods
verification_status: confirmed - China-Global South Project (based on Chinese customs data), OEC, SAIS-CARI, Lowy Institute

2025_bilateral_trade.slowdown_cause: the DRC's cobalt export ban, introduced in February 2025 - direct evidence that Kinshasa's regulatory moves genuinely affect trade flows
2025_bilateral_trade.source: China-Global South Project (chinaglobalsouth.com), February 2026, based on China's General Administration of Customs

reverse_flow_snapshot_may_2026.conclusion: a closed loop in its purest form: the DRC ships refined copper and gets back finished batteries, transformers, and wire made from that same copper - but now with someone else's value added. The growth in Chinese exports in exactly these categories is quantitative proof that value creation is not happening in Congo.

credit_context.chinas_role_reversal: per the Lowy Institute, China has shifted from the developing world's largest lender to its main debt collector: debt service owed to China totaled $35bn in 2025 overall and $22bn from the poorest countries
credit_context.drc_exception: the DRC is in a narrow group of countries still receiving NEW Chinese lending - alongside Argentina, Brazil, and Indonesia - precisely because it exports critical minerals
credit_context.china_lending_to_africa: $4.61bn in 2023 (the first increase in years) versus a regular $10bn+ at the BRI's peak; a total of 1,306 loans worth $182.28bn to 49 countries over 2000-2023
credit_context.significance: the model has shifted: fewer sovereign loans, more projects repaid through commodity flows and equity stakes - exactly what Sicomines, TAZARA, and Nzilo II describe
